verdict.rationale: First-party docs show the YubiKey ships its own legacy OTP capabilities. These are an OATH application whose shared secrets are stored and processed in the secure element, configurable OATH/OTP slots via ykman, HOTP and Yubico OTP retrievable over NFC, and Yubico OTP that types as a plain string without client software. TOTP is never named explicitly, and nothing documents challenge-response, so the story's coverage is only partial. missing for 10: explicit TOTP documentation, challenge-response mode evidence, independent hands-on corroboration of OTP/OATH use with non-WebAuthn services.

support.subject: As a power user, the key covers legacy one-time-password schemes — TOTP/HOTP slots or challenge-response — for services that still lack WebAuthn

citations.quote: the shared secrets are stored and processed in the YubiKey's secure element
provides the APIs to request an OTP (Yubico OTP or HOTP) from the NFC YubiKeys using a NFC-enabled iOS device
Full scriptable device management: enable applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots, device info.
No client software needed. The OTP is just a string. If you can send a password, you can send an OTP.
